skill.name: microsoft-teams-automation
skill.description: Guide AI agents to automate Microsoft Teams tasks through Rube MCP, including messages, chats, meetings, channel management, and search.
skill.summary: Guides Microsoft Teams automation through Rube MCP tool sequences, IDs, permissions, and operational pitfalls.

security_audit.summary: Reviewed SKILL.md context for all 60 static findings. The command hits are Markdown formatting around tool names or parameters. The URL and reconnaissance hits are normal Rube MCP setup, Teams ID guidance, and permission guidance.

static_findings.snippet: - Active Microsoft Teams connection via `RUBE_MANAGE_CONNECTIONS` with toolkit `microsoft_teams`
- Always call `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` first to get current tool schemas
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
1. Verify Rube MCP is available by confirming `RUBE_SEARCH_TOOLS` responds
1. `MICROSOFT_TEAMS_TEAMS_LIST` - List teams to find target team [Prerequisite]
- `end_date_time`: ISO 8601 end time (must be after start)
- `participants`: Array of user objects with user_id and role
2. `MICROSOFT_TEAMS_GET_TEAM` - Get details for a specific team [Optional]
7. `MICROSOFT_TEAMS_ADD_MEMBER_TO_TEAM` - Add a member to the team [Optional]
- `query`: KQL search query (supports from:, sent:, attachments, boolean logic)
**Get Rube MCP**: Add `https://rube.app/mcp` as an MCP server in your client configuration. No API k
- team_id must be a valid UUID format
- channel_id must be in thread format (e.g., '19:abc@thread.tacv2')
- `participants`: Array of user objects with user_id and role
- Participants require valid Microsoft user_id (GUID) values, not emails
- GET_CHANNEL returns 404 if team_id or channel_id is wrong
| Add team member | MICROSOFT_TEAMS_ADD_MEMBER_TO_TEAM | team_id, user_id |
| Get chat message | MICROSOFT_TEAMS_GET_CHAT_MESSAGE | chat_id, message_id |
- 403 errors indicate insufficient permissions or team access

content.value_statement: Microsoft Teams tasks often require precise IDs, permissions, and tool order. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code repeatable Rube MCP workflows for Teams messaging, meetings, channels, and search.
actual_capabilities: Connects Teams workflows through Rube MCP and Microsoft Teams toolkit authentication.
Lists teams, channels, chats, users, and team members before actions.
Posts messages to channels or chats with text or HTML content.
Creates Teams meetings with subject, start time, end time, and participants.
Creates channels, adds members, gets details, and searches Teams messages.
Explains pagination, throttling, ID formats, and permission errors.
limitations: Requires Rube MCP and an active Microsoft Teams OAuth connection.
Actions are limited by Microsoft Graph permissions and tenant admin consent.
Search results can lag because Teams indexing is eventually consistent.
Calendar-linked meetings require Outlook calendar tooling, not this meeting workflow.

use_cases.title: Post Channel Updates
use_cases.description: Send routine announcements after resolving the right team and channel IDs.

use_cases.title: Schedule Team Meetings
use_cases.description: Create Teams meetings with accurate participant IDs and validated start and end times.

use_cases.title: Manage Teams Access
use_cases.description: List teams, inspect channels, add members, and handle permission errors during support tasks.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Channel Message
prompt_templates.prompt: Find the team named Engineering, find its General channel, and post this message: The deployment window starts at 18:00 UTC.

prompt_templates.title: Send a Direct Chat Update
prompt_templates.prompt: Find an existing chat with Priya Shah. If none exists, create a one-on-one chat and send the status update I provide.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Teams Meeting
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a Teams meeting for the incident review with Alex Lee and Morgan Chen on the date I provide from 15:00 to 15:30 UTC.

prompt_templates.title: Search and Summarize Messages
prompt_templates.prompt: Search Teams messages for deployment blockers from the last seven days, summarize likely owners, and cite the channels or chats found.

output_examples.input: Send a launch update to the Marketing team general channel.
output: Resolved the Marketing team and General channel.
Posted the launch update as a text message.
Reported any Teams permission or throttling errors.

output_examples.input: Schedule a customer review meeting for three participants.
output: Found participant user IDs from Teams users.
Created the meeting with the requested subject and time window.
Returned the meeting join details and noted calendar limitations.

output_examples.input: Search for recent messages about access issues.
output: Ran a Teams message search using the requested terms.
Grouped matching messages by chat or channel.
Summarized permission-related findings without changing Teams data.

best_practices: Confirm the Rube MCP connection is active before using Teams tools.
Resolve team, channel, chat, and user IDs from list tools before actions.
Use small batches and backoff when Microsoft Graph returns throttling errors.
anti_patterns: Do not guess Teams IDs from display names or message URLs.
Do not send bulk messages without tenant approval and clear user intent.
Do not assume Teams search reflects messages posted in the last minute.

faq.question: Does this skill need a Microsoft Teams account?
faq.answer: Yes. It requires an authenticated Teams connection through Rube MCP.

faq.question: Can it send messages to channels and chats?
faq.answer: Yes. It guides channel messages, direct chats, and group chat messages.

faq.question: Can it create calendar events?
faq.answer: No. It creates standalone Teams meetings. Calendar events require Outlook calendar tooling.

faq.question: Does it expose API keys?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents OAuth through Rube MCP and does not include secrets.

faq.question: Can it manage team members?
faq.answer: Yes, when the connected account has the required Microsoft Graph permissions.

faq.question: Why must it search tools first?
faq.answer: Rube MCP schemas can change. Searching first helps the agent use current parameters.
